craft_playbook: Deliver the hook inside 2.5 seconds; viewers decide in under 2 on mobile.
Open with a pattern interrupt or curiosity gap; NEVER context/build-up or greetings.
Reverse structure: lead with the payoff (news, boldest number, verdict tease), explain after.
Include a concrete number in the hook when possible (price, 0-100, sales figure).
No dead air: trim silences; keep delivery slightly faster than conversational.
Bury nothing: the best moment goes first, not 15 seconds in.
One idea per beat; cut visuals every 2-3 seconds; open on motion or high-contrast frame.
End with a question that begs a comment + a loop-friendly closer (last line can feed the first).
Hook and content must match; clickbait mismatch kills retention and trust.
Front-load value beats: price/verdict by the midpoint, never last.
data_learnings: [high][owner-feedback] Peak-beat humor reads flat — jokes must be specific roasts/analogies, not generic; punch-up pass should rewrite any joke that could apply to any car.
[medium][owner-feedback] Visual mismatch persists on news/value beats when the pool lacks true subject footage — prefer neutral scenery over near-miss car shots.
QA auto-fix works for true peak ≤ -1 dBTP via re-polish with extra headroom; keep gains conservative on punchy voices.

[high][owner-feedback] On-screen text = word-synced highlight pops ONLY: each pop is a word-exact fragment of the narration and renders exactly while those words are spoken (TTS word marks). Max 2 per beat, never stacked. Writers should fill segment `pops` with the 1-2 strongest fragments per beat (figures, names, punchline objects).
[high][owner-feedback] Add more text overlays in sections discussing specs or news to enhance viewer engagement and provide additional context.
[high][owner-feedback] add more text overlays from each section where specs or news is discussed to enhance viewer engagement and provide additional information
